project_summary.name: Clinic No-Show Case Study
project_summary.objective: Prioritize appointment confirmation outreach for no-show risk

data_quality_changes.rule: keep first occurrence of each appointment_id

key_insights.finding: Eligible no-show rate is 14.4% (cancellations 12.5% of all bookings).
key_insights.operational_implication: Reminder capacity should target the eligible universe, not cancelled slots.

key_insights.finding: No-show rises with lead time (0-3d: 6.7% on n=15; 15-30d: 15.3%). The 31+ bucket is too sparse to interpret (n=2).
key_insights.operational_implication: Longer booking horizons remain priority candidates for confirmation outreach.
key_insights.caveat: Pattern was intentionally injected by the generator; extreme buckets may be sparse.

key_insights.operational_implication: Channel-specific reminder scripts may be warranted in a live setting.
key_insights.caveat: Synthetic association; not causal proof that phone booking causes no-shows.

key_insights.finding: Dermatology (17.2%) and gynecology (16.3%) sit above pediatrics (10.6%).
key_insights.operational_implication: Specialty-level staffing buffers differ; avoid one-size-fits-all overbooking.
key_insights.caveat: One professional per specialty in this synthetic design.

key_insights.finding: Patients with prior no-shows show elevated risk versus first-visit and clean repeats.
key_insights.operational_implication: History-aware prioritization is more actionable than demographics alone.
key_insights.caveat: History features are generator-aligned and known before the visit.

limitations: Scores not fully calibrated; use for ranking
No clinical prediction or causal claims
